title: Security questionnaire workshop template and answer bank
content:
Purpose
This doc is a lightweight workshop template + answer bank for customer security questionnaires. Target use: pre-sales and customer security calls where we need an operational runbook for: (1) drafting concise Q&A, (2) mapping canned evidence, and (3) creating a follow-up pack with extracts for SIEM/audit-log questions.

Status and audience
- Status: draft (working master for SEs and security eng).
- Audience: Solutions engineering, security reviewers, customer security teams, and account leads preparing questionnaire responses.

High-level goals for a session
1) Surface the subset of questions the customer will definitely ask (RBAC, audit logging, data retention, export formats).
2) Agree on standard short-form answers + reference evidence files we can attach.
3) Identify items requiring engineering work or custom extracts (e.g., sampling audit-log exports, anonymized payloads).

Recommended workshop agenda (90 minutes)
- 00:00–00:10: Kickoff: objectives, participants, SLAs for follow-up
- 00:10–00:35: Rapid-fire Q categorization (card-sorting): RBAC / Audit logs / SIEM export / KMS & keys / Data retention & deletion / Compliance requests
- 00:35–00:55: Answer drafting: produce short answer (1–3 lines) + reference evidence pointer for each high-priority Q
- 00:55–01:10: Evidence planning: identify any data extracts or logs needed, owners, and anonymization plan
- 01:10–01:30: Next steps, owners, timeline, and escalation path

Template for each questionnaire item (use this block in the meeting)
- QID: unique id (e.g., Q-001)
- Question (verbatim): 
- Short answer (customer-facing, 1–3 lines):
- Long answer (internal, technical):
- Evidence attachments (what to include):
- Owner (who will gather/produce):
- ETA: date or sprint
- Risk/notes: open items or follow-ups (e.g., PII in logs, cross-tenant exports)

Example items and canonical answers (answer bank)
Q-001: Describe access control model and role design for user and service accounts
- Short answer: We use a role-based access control (RBAC v2) model where permissions are assigned to roles; roles are bound to users, service principals, and API keys. Administrative roles are restricted and audited.
- Long answer: RBAC v2 supports hierarchical role composition and resource-scoped role bindings. Roles are defined in our control plane (private or hosted) and enforced at the request router. Service-to-service tokens use short-lived credentials with optional mTLS. Role changes are versioned and immutable once recorded in the audit log (see Q-005 for schema).
- Evidence attachments: role definition export (CSV), sample role-binding JSON (sanitized), RBAC change audit log extract (1 week, sampled)
- Owner: eng/authorization (Ethan Wu)
- ETA: 3 business days
- Risk/notes: need to sanitize user identifiers before sharing with customers; add explanation of default-deny policies.

Q-002: How do you capture and store audit logs? What fields are available?
- Short answer: We emit structured audit events for authentication, authorization, admin-config changes, and model-serving requests. Logs are stored encrypted in append-only storage with retention controls and export hooks for SIEM.
- Long answer: The audit-log schema is event-based JSON. Top-level fields include timestamp, event_type, actor_id (hashed if exported), actor_type, resource_id, action, request_id, request_path, response_code, latency_ms, model_variant, region, and metadata (freeform key-value). Log writes are atomic and the storage backend supports immutability settings for compliance customers.
- Evidence attachments: sample audit-log JSON lines (sanitized), schema doc (CSV field list), retention policy excerpt
- Owner: observability (Gabriela Martinez)
- ETA: 48 hours

Q-003: Can we stream logs to our SIEM? What formats and protocols are supported?
- Short answer: Yes — we support push (HTTPS JSON batches) and pull (S3 snapshots) delivery modes; common SIEM integrations include Splunk, Datadog, and customer-managed S3 connectors.
- Long answer: We provide a configurable SIEM export adapter with options for event batching, gzipped newline-delimited JSON, and field-mapping templates. Optionally we can deliver to a customer-owned S3 bucket with lifecycle/retention settings or set up an HTTPS webhook with HMAC-signed payloads.
- Evidence attachments: sample export manifest, transport spec, and mapping table
- Owner: observability/integrations (Noah Kim)
- ETA: 5 business days for custom mappings; standard templates immediate
- Risk/notes: need to confirm customer’s ingestion format for timestamp precision and field names.

Q-004: What anonymization/pseudonymization options are available for exported audit logs?
- Short answer: We can hash or redact sensitive fields (actor_id, user_email) and provide deterministic pseudonyms for correlation when requested.
- Long answer: Export pipelines can apply transformation rules: full redaction, SHA-256 hashing, or tokenization via a customer-provided KMS. We document the fields we consider sensitive and provide an export preview pipeline for customer sign-off.
- Evidence attachments: transform config example, anonymized sample, policy doc
- Owner: privacy-compliance (Asha Patel)
- ETA: 2–3 business days for sample exports

Q-005: Where can I find the audit log schema and an explanation of each field?
- Short answer: See attached schema CSV and the short field glossary below.
- Long answer: (internal) The attached schema CSV lists every field, type, and whether it is exported by default or only for enterprise customers. Fields of note: request_id (UUID), event_type (enum), actor.identity (object — hashed), resource.path, result.code, latency_ms, kv_changes (optional), model.hash
- Evidence attachments: schema CSV, field glossary one-pager
- Owner: observability docs (Gabriela Martinez)
- ETA: immediate (document is attached)

Field glossary (short)
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC timestamp
- request_id: unique per request
- event_type: auth|authz|admin|invoke|error|system
- actor_id: internal id (hashed in exports)
- resource_id: resource or model identifier
- action: create|update|delete|read|invoke
- model_variant: model id and revision serving inference
- latency_ms: execution latency in milliseconds

Evidence automation patterns (practical notes)
- Provide a single ZIP per customer with: sanitized sample logs (3 days), schema CSV, role export CSV, and a short README.
- For frequent requests, create a job in github.com/redwood-inference/security-evidence-scripts to assemble artifacts and push to a signed S3 link.
- Automate PII redaction with a config-driven pipeline: regex rules + structured-field blacklist + deterministic hashing for correlatability.

Attachments we usually include in a customer pack
- Schema CSV
- 3-day sample audit log (sanitized)
- Role definitions export
- SIEM mapping template (Splunk/Datadog example)
- Evidence checklist (who signed off)

Open questions / engineering work
- Sampling policy: decide default sampling rate for production customers who request sample logs (current ad-hoc approach is inconsistent). Owner: observability.
- Export performance: creating large S3 snapshots for customers can be throttled; need SLA language. Owner: infra.
- RBAC v2 docs: need an illustrated diagram for role inheritance — product documentation ticket created.

Quick talk tracks (for SEs)
- 30s elevator: "We record structured, tamper-evident audit events for control plane and data plane operations and can deliver them to your SIEM in JSON or S3 with configurable anonymization."
- Deep dive (3–5 min): describe the schema, field-level controls, and the export path (how we sign and deliver snapshots).

Follow-ups / next steps after workshop
- Produce a customer-pack ZIP (owner listed per Q) and upload to a signed link.
- If customer needs continuous streaming, open integrations ticket (JIRA) and assign to integrations team.
- Record any policy exceptions in the security exceptions register.

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep language non-PII when generating sample logs.
- Add a short explainer about model_variant — common confusion point for customers asking about inference-level logs.
- Cross-link to trust artifacts: policies on retention, immutable logs, and KMS options.

Revision history
- 2025-11-03: created (Asha Patel)
- 2026-01-15: added SIEM templates + field glossary (Gabriela Martinez)
- 2026-03-01: refined answers and added evidence automation pattern (Noah Kim)

End of doc
